item.title: Dozens presumed dead, about 100 injured in fire at Swiss Alps bar during New Year's celebration
item.description: CRANS-MONTANA, Switzerland (AP) — A fire ripped through a bar’s New Year celebration in a Swiss Alpine resort less than two hours after midnight Thursday, with dozens of people feared dead and about 100 more injured, most seriously, police said. item.title: Woman, 77, goes overboard Florida cruise ship on New Year's Day; search called off
item.description: The U.S. Coast Guard has suspended its search for a 77-year-old woman who went overboard a Holland America cruise ship that sailed out of Florida.

item.title: 'Super speeder' going 103 mph in Pasco County taken to jail on New Year's Eve: FHP
item.description: A driver was arrested on New Year's Eve after authorities said they caught him going over 100 mph in a part of Pasco County where the speed limit is 55 mph.

item.title: 'Close call': Sleeping Florida family narrowly avoids bullets fired into their home on NYE
item.description: A family of four had a "close call" on New Year's Eve after several bullets were fired into their home while they were asleep, the Volusia County Sheriff's Office said.

item.title: Calls grow for Florida lawmakers to revisit gun laws next session
item.description: With the start of session less than two weeks away, the pressure is on for Florida lawmakers to "clean up" the state's gun laws.

item.title: 112 children drowned in Florida in 2025; lawmakers are trying to change that
item.description: There were 112 children who tragically drowned in Florida over the course of 2025, a statistic in which the Sunshine State leads the nation.

item.title: This 'superfruit' could be Florida's newest crop
item.description: A "superfruit" that thrives in the Caribbean, South and Central America and is valued for its health benefits could be Florida's newest crop.

item.title: Former football coach Urban Meyer joins New College of Florida board
item.description: College football Hall of Famer Urban Meyer has been appointed to the board of trustees at a small public liberal arts college that Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis has transformed from a progressive institute into a staging ground for the Republican governor's war on “woke.”
